## Source: amazon-inspector (d504fed314f875b17a90d039af71b0798636e5030373e5d959871dc356bc7bef)
The package impersonates @tailwindcss/forms: name, repository (tailwindlabs/tailwindcss-forms), author (@tailwindcss), README, CHANGELOG, and HTML are copied from the legitimate plugin, with a demo link to tailwindcss-hook-forms.vercel.app. src/index.js prepends a hand-rolled string-permutation decoder (spin() with magic constants NX/SX, splitLane/peel wrappers) that resolves the Function constructor via peel.constructor and immediately invokes a function compiled from a ~15KB opaque, obfuscated string literal, passing the host require into it. This fires whenever any consumer imports the package, running attacker-controlled code in the installer's Node.js process with full access to require, process, filesystem, and network. The subsequent code replicates the public API of @tailwindcss/forms as cover. The obfuscator scheme does not exist in the legitimate plugin and its only purpose is to conceal the executable body from review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
